title: I work the night drive-thru. The lane sensor says a car has been waiting since midnight.
transcript:
I work the night drive-thru. The lane sensor says a car has been waiting since midnight. "Hello? Are you ready to order?" Nobody answered. But the headset hissed in my ear, slow and steady, like someone breathing right into the speaker.

I work the drive-thru alone from eleven to six. A sensor beeps when a car pulls up to the menu board. At midnight, it beeped. The lane camera showed nothing but rain on empty pavement.

It's three now. The beeping never stopped. Whatever pulled in has been sitting there for three hours.

Then the voice came, low and friendly. "Sorry. I'm still deciding."

I stared at the camera feed. No car. Nobody. Just the menu board, glowing in the rain. My manager wasn't picking up. So I did the only thing I could think of. I shut off the lane lights and pulled the headset off.

The sensor went silent. The lot went dark. And in the quiet, I could still hear it. That slow, steady breathing.

It wasn't coming from the speaker. It was right behind my left ear, close enough to feel.

"Sorry," it whispered. "I'm still deciding."

It had never been in the lane.
